newsitem.title: UK: UK TV advertising sales house forms new media arm.
newsitem.headline: UK TV advertising sales house forms new media arm.

text.p: TSMS, the largest advertising sales house for Britain's ITV television network, on Thursday said it formed a new unit to sell advertising on the Internet and other new media.

TSMSi, the newly formed unit of United News & Media Plc's TSMS, will initially focus on tapping the advertising potential of the Internet, the vast international network of computer data bases whose commercial World Wide Web sites now number in the millions.

Advertising on the Internet remains in its infancy, but it is expected to grow rapidly. British companies in 1996 spent less than one million pounds on Internet advertising, but TSMS said that figure is expected to rise to close to 90 million pounds by 2000.

TSMSi is forming alliances with Web site design firms, research companies and consultancies as part of its strategy to sell advertising on the Internet, company intranets, CD-ROMs, interactive television and on interactive kiosks.
"We believe the way the market will develop is through the building of long-term business alliances," Paul Simon, general manager of TSMSi, told a news conference.

"What we basically have as a business is an investment," said Jerry Hill, chief executive of TSMS. Hill said the company was not looking to turn profitable in the short term, "but we do have a relatively optimistic view about the future of new media."
Hill described TSMS' investment in the new unit as "a six-figure number. But it is not millions."
TSMSi will initially focus on Web site advertising, but is looking beyond that for the future.
"Advertising sales on the Web is the key issue at the moment," Simon said. "But we all know that other technologies in the medium- and long-term are to grow even more rapidly."

Simon cited Intranets -- private Internet sites designed for companies, and CD-ROMs among new media that offer promising advertising opportunities. Although the CD-ROM market has been going through a shake-out, he said it continued to hold solid long-term potential and was ripe for advertising opportunities.

TSMSi will sell advertising and sponsorship space on Web sites by packaging together compatible Web sites and selling the packages to advertisers. The company has compiled six packages, including Captains of Industry, for sites targeted at senior managers; Musical Youth, targeting 15- to 34-year olds; The Professionals, aimed at ABC1s in a business environment; The Smarter Investors, targeting ABs; Campus, for 18- to 34-year-olds and students, and Middle England, targeting adult Bs, C1s and C2s.
TSMSi will initially focus on advertisers with Web site advertising budgets in the six figures.
"We are very clear of which brands have substantial, six-figure budgets for new media advertising," he said.

In addition, TSMSi aims to move beyond the banner advertising that currently dominates Web sites, including offering Web site sponsorship deals. "I think the thing is to reinvent the whole process of how the content provider and the advertiser work together," Simon said.
